title: Rosalind and the Witness
premise: Insurance investigator Noor Reyes is hired by a wealthy matriarch, Rosalind Ashcombe, to prove that her late gardener's death was natural — before the family's anniversary dinner, where Rosalind intends to publicly name her heir. But Noor's photographic memory catches contradictions in the estate's records: the 'dead' man, Mateo, may still be alive, and someone inside Ashcombe House has been erasing him from every ledger, photograph, and memory. As Noor digs, they realize they were hired not to close a case but to be framed for opening it — Rosalind wants a disposable outsider to take the fall when the truth surfaces. In the end, Noor finds Mateo hiding in plain sight as the estate's night watchman, exposes Rosalind's decades-long theft of his inheritance, and chooses the found family of servants who protected him over the case file itself.
about_author: Theo Vane is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet crimes, and the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: Paid in Full, Up Front
chapters.summary: Noor Reyes, POV. A retainer arrives with no return address: prove Rosalind Ashcombe's gardener died of natural causes, fee doubled if closed before the anniversary dinner. Noor, who never takes an unclosable case, accepts out of pride. Emotional beat: confidence curdling into unease when the payment clears through a shell company tied to the estate itself.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. At Ashcombe House, staff offer rehearsed grief; the widow offers champagne. Noor's memory flags it: three staff describe Mateo's funeral, but each names a different date. Emotional beat: the first crack — Noor realizes the household isn't lying badly, they're lying in unison, which takes coordination.

chapters.title: A Photograph With One Person Missing
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. The estate archive shows a group photo of staff on the lawn; the negative reveals a cropped silhouette beside Rosalind. Someone excised a man from the record. Emotional beat: thrill of the hunt shadowed by dread — whoever edited the photo had access, authority, and time.

chapters.title: Rosalind Explains Everything Twice
chapters.summary: Rosalind, POV. The matriarch rehearses her version of Mateo's death like a monologue, aware the investigator is watching her hands. She reveals a sliver of truth: Mateo knew something about the family money. Emotional beat: we see Rosalind's charm as a weapon, and her fear that the dinner — her legacy — will be interrupted.

chapters.title: The Night Watchman Who Never Speaks
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. A silent groundskeeper avoids eye contact, wears gloves indoors, and flinches at Mateo's name. Noor's memory matches his gait to the cropped photograph. Emotional beat: recognition without proof — the witness everyone swears is dead walks the halls at night.

chapters.title: Ledgers, Lies, and a Burned Page
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Payroll records show wages paid to 'M. Vidal' for six years after his supposed death — then a burned gap. Noor confronts the housekeeper, Delia, who begs them to stop. Emotional beat: Noor realizes the servants aren't concealing a murder; they're protecting a living man.

chapters.title: What the Anniversary Dinner Is Really For
chapters.summary: Rosalind, POV. Preparations intensify; Rosalind drafts the speech naming her heir and instructs her lawyer that 'the investigator matter' must resolve cleanly by Friday. Emotional beat: cold clarity — Rosalind hired Noor as a scapegoat, a stranger whose snooping can be blamed when Mateo's claim surfaces.

chapters.title: The Cellar and the Confession
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Cornered by Rosalind's son-in-law, Noor escapes into the wine cellar and finds Mateo's hidden room: letters proving he is Rosalind's half-brother, cheated of his inheritance forty years ago. Emotional beat: the case inverts — Noor wasn't hired to prove a death but to bury a life.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Noor and Mateo, alternating POV. At the anniversary dinner, Rosalind raises her glass to legacy while Noor stands and reads Mateo's letters aloud. The staff, one by one, confirm what they've carried in silence for decades. Emotional beat: climax — power exposed at its own celebration, the found family choosing truth together.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Rosalind faces ruin; Mateo declines the fortune, asking only for his name restored to the payroll he never stopped earning. Noor closes the case their own way — report filed, client fired, and a standing invitation to Sunday dinner at the gatehouse. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging isn't found in records; it's found in who stands up when your name is read aloud.
